subject: research/osrobot-mjface
professional: a robotics simulation researcher working on physical human-robot interaction safety (MuJoCo contact modelling, ISO/TS 15066 power-and-force limiting, assistive feeding). They would check first that the contact parameters fed to the simulator are the physical quantities the README says they are (MuJoCo's direct solref (-k, -b) is a reference acceleration, so per unit effective mass, not N/m and N s/m), then that the simulated transient peak agrees with the standard's own Annex A energy-transfer model F = v*sqrt(k*mu), and only then the force-limit comparison and the missing pressure limits

evidence.correctness: Reproducibility is fine: in a scratch copy (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4d40ef56-18b0-5820-a3ae-5a4c926539dc/scratchpad/mjface/copy) `/usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/run.py` (mujoco 4.0.1) ran in 51 s and results.txt differs from the committed file only in the header's MuJoCo version (3.16.0 there); every data row is identical, and figure.py regenerates a byte-identical peak_force.svg. The physics is not what the README says. (1) Independent check of the upstream library's contact law with no subject code (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4d40ef56-18b0-5820-a3ae-5a4c926539dc/scratchpad/mjface/units.py): a free sphere hitting a mocap box at 0.10 m/s with solref (-k, -0.001) peaks at 0.871/8.711 N (k=800, m=0.3/3 kg) and 8.296/82.955 N (k=75000), matching m*v*sqrt(k) (0.849/8.485/8.216/82.158) and not v*sqrt(k*m) (1.549/4.899/15.000/47.434): the peak scales with m, so MuJoCo's direct solref is a mass-normalised (acceleration) stiffness and damping, as MuJoCo's documented aref = -b*(Jv) - k*imp*r says. With the tip mass 0.30 kg against an immovable mocap lip, the simulated face stiffness is 0.3 x 75,000 = 22,500 N/m (22.5 N/mm, not ISO/TS 15066's 75 N/mm) and every b is 0.3x the stated N s/m. (2) ISO/TS 15066 Annex A transient model, F = v*sqrt(k*mu), mu = (1/0.30 + 1/4.4)^-1 = 0.281 kg (face/head effective mass 4.4 kg): 14.51 N at 0.10 m/s and 29.03 N at 0.20 m/s, against the reported 7.56 and 15.21 N. Re-running the subject's own trial with solref scaled by 1/M_TIP so k and b are the stated force-domain values (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4d40ef56-18b0-5820-a3ae-5a4c926539dc/scratchpad/mjface/corrected.py) gives 11.86/23.82 N at b=4, 85.67/171.64 N blocked at b=1000 (reported 24.62/49.25), and for the camera arm at 0.20 m/s, b=1000: safe<=65 N share 0.48 (reported 1.00), mean 80.0 N, worst 203.7 N (reported 53.3 N, above the 130 N limit too). corrected2.py: at b=4/100 the 1.00 shares survive (worst 24-38 N); at the README's 'critical' b=300 worst is 68.3 N and safe<=65 is 0.98 at 0.20 m/s. (3) README 'critical value 300 N s/m for the 0.30 kg tip at 75,000 N/m' is 2*sqrt(k*m) = 300 in force units, but in the units actually fed to MuJoCo critical is 2*sqrt(k) = 547.7, so the sweep's 300 is zeta 0.55, not 1. (4) Hand arithmetic that does pass: KP*LEAD*v = 400*0.05*0.10 = 2.0 N steady push (test and results agree); 7.56/3.68 = 2.05 and 15.21/7.35 = 2.07 ('about 2x'); 75000/800 = 93.75 ('94-fold'); 53.3/65 = 0.82; 65/2 = 32.5 and 130/2 = 65 ('30 to 65x'). Numbers reproduce from the code, but the headline peaks are understated 1.6x (b=4) to 3.5x (b=1000) and the 'all safe' row flips: 1.

evidence.craft: Read experiments/run.py (40 lines), experiments/figure.py, tests/test_face.py, and the imported research/osrobot-mjfeed/src/osrobot_mjfeed/model.py (121 lines). Small, readable, deterministic, reuses the sibling model unchanged as intended. Defects: the dependency is a sys.path insert into a sibling project with no pyproject or pinned mujoco version (README says 3.16.0; 4.0.1 installed here and gave the same rows, by luck not by pin); K_FACE duplicated in run.py:14 and tests/test_face.py:6; experiment logic in run.py has no tests at all; the solref values are written as '-{k} -{b}' with a comment calling them N/m and N s/m (mjfeed model.py:13) with no conversion by effective mass; run.py:4 'a few minutes' vs README '90 s' vs 51 s measured: 2.
evidence.claims: Backed: disclaimer and 'not a safety case', secondary-source caveat on the ISO table values, unsourced damping, pressure limits not applied, kinematic lips, AI-assistance note, all numbers in the README match results.txt. Not backed: README:3 title and project.json 'when the lips have the ISO/TS 15066 face stiffness' and README table 'Face effective spring constant 75,000 N/m' are false in physical units (simulated 22,500 N/m, see correctness); README:19 '300 N s/m is the critical value' is wrong for the units used (547.7); README:11 'nowhere near unsafe in this model' and 'worst case 53.3 N, 82% of 65 N' do not survive the unit correction (204 N, safe share 0.48 at b=1000) and are stated while pressure limits, which the README itself says may bind first for a 4 mm tip, were not checked; README:10 '2x, not 94x' sets up a strawman: no model predicts 94x, a linear spring impact (and ISO/TS 15066 Annex A) predicts sqrt(94) = 9.7x, so the right framing is 2x against the 9.7x the standard's own model gives. A reader would act on the safety reading: 1.
evidence.fitness: Job: could a pHRI or assistive-feeding researcher build on 'with the standard's face stiffness the feeding arm stays under the face force limits'? No: the stiffness and damping are mis-scaled by the tip mass, so the conclusion holds only at low damping (b <= 100 force-domain, worst 38 N) and fails at the swept b=1000 (worst 204 N). The useful residue is the observation that the old 2 N limit, not the contact physics, drove osrobot-mjfeed's 'unsafe' reading, which is arithmetic on the limits (65/2 = 32.5x) and needs no simulation. Nearest prior work, none cited beyond the standard: ISO/TS 15066:2016 Annex A itself (the energy-transfer transient model F = v*sqrt(k*mu) that would have served as the baseline and exposed the factor), Haddadin, Albu-Schaeffer and Hirzinger (2009) 'Requirements for safe robots' (impact peaks vs speed and effective mass), Kirschner et al. on experimental ISO/TS 15066 power-and-force limiting, MuJoCo's own documentation of solref direct mode, and robot-assisted feeding work with contact-force limits (Gallenberger et al. 2019 bite transfer; Bhattacharjee et al. 2020; Erickson et al. 2020 Assistive Gym, whose feeding task penalises contact force). The result is not new (a parameter sweep of an existing toy model) and not sound as stated: 1.
evidence.domain: Compared against MuJoCo contact-modelling practice (solref direct mode is per unit effective mass; practitioners convert a physical k by dividing by the effective mass, or calibrate against a drop test) and ISO/TS 15066 PFL practice (transient peak from the Annex A energy model with body-region effective mass, compared to the transient limit, plus the pressure limits). Right: using the standard's body-region force limits rather than an invented comfort threshold; sweeping the unsourced damping; flagging that the tables came from secondary sources; noting the rigid kinematic face is an upper-end case. Departures: physical k and b fed as acceleration-domain parameters (a 0.3x error on both); no comparison with the standard's own transient formula; face transient limit treated as ambiguous and both 65 and 130 N used without the pressure check that would bind first for a 4 mm sphere; the 75 N/mm body-region spring constant applied to a point contact (acknowledged). A practitioner would not sign off the method until the parameter mapping is fixed and validated against the analytic impact: 1.

defects.what: Contact stiffness and damping are passed to MuJoCo's direct solref (-k, -b), which is mass-normalised (reference acceleration), as if they were N/m and N s/m. With the 0.30 kg tip against an immovable mocap lip the simulated face stiffness is 22,500 N/m, not ISO/TS 15066's 75,000, and every damping is 0.3x its label. Peaks are understated 1.6x (b=4: 7.56 vs 11.86 N at 0.10 m/s; ISO Annex A gives 14.5 N) to 3.5x (b=1000); the camera-arm 0.20 m/s b=1000 row becomes 0.48 safe at 65 N with a 204 N worst peak instead of 1.00 and 53.3 N.

Headline safety reading 'nowhere near unsafe ... 1.00 in every row, worst 53.3 N' (README, project.json lede, live page) rests on the mis-scaled parameters and on force limits alone while the pressure limits, which the README says may bind first for a 4 mm tip, were not applied.

No baseline against the standard's own transient model F = v*sqrt(k*mu); the '2x, not 94x' framing compares with a scaling no model predicts (a spring impact predicts sqrt(94) = 9.7x). The analytic check would have exposed the units factor.
'300 N s/m is the critical value' is computed in force units (2*sqrt(k*m)) but fed to MuJoCo in per-unit-mass units, where critical is 2*sqrt(k) = 548; the swept b=300 is zeta 0.55.
Tests never touch experiments/run.py and pin no absolute force; 4 of 5 seeded mutations survived (limit applied to the axial component, K_FACE 10x lower, p95 as median, controller damping halved).
Runtime and version drift: run.py docstring 'a few minutes', README 'about 90 s', measured 51 s; mujoco version stated (3.16.0) but not pinned, no pyproject for this project.

verdict: Reproducible and honestly caveated, but wrong at the core: the 'ISO/TS 15066 face stiffness' is fed to MuJoCo's direct solref, which is per unit effective mass, so the simulated face is 22.5 N/mm and every damping is 0.3x its label (units.py: peak scales with m, 8.30 N at 0.3 kg and 82.96 N at 3 kg, not with sqrt(m)). Converting k and b by the 0.30 kg tip mass raises the 0.10 m/s blocked peak from 7.56 to 11.86 N (the standard's own Annex A model gives 14.5 N) and turns the b=1000 camera row from 1.00 safe/53.3 N worst to 0.48 safe/204 N worst. The low-damping rows still clear 65 N, and the point that the invented 2 N limit drove osrobot-mjfeed's 'unsafe' reading stands, but the README's safety reading, the critical-damping value and the '2x not 94x' framing do not. Tests check ratios of the imported model and never run run.py; 4 of 5 seeded mutations survived. Does not meet the bar.
